svg.title: Approve and return the renewal certificate — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Approve and return the renewal certificate
Practice CA server (TLS-CA01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.20
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-ca01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
cd ~/tls-ca
openssl req -in incoming/app-r1.csr -noout -verify -subject
openssl x509 -req -in incoming/app-r1.csr -CA intermediate.crt -CAkey intermediate.key -CAserial
intermediate.srl -CAcreateserial -days 90 -sha256 -extfile server.ext -out issued/app-r1.crt
openssl x509 -in issued/app-r1.crt -noout -serial -dates
cp issued/app-r1.crt public/
chmod 644 public/app-r1.crt
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
A newly signed app-r1.crt has a new serial. notAfter may differ only slightly in this fast
practice renewal.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. At the CA terminal, inspect app-r1.csr and repeat the same-name approval check.
2. Sign using the intermediate and its existing serial file. Do not recreate the root or intermediate
CA.
3. Copy the new public leaf into the response folder. Compare its serial with the older leaf: they
should differ even though issuance may happen the same day.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
